intro: RTF to PDF converts Rich Text Format documents into PDF. RTF is an old but widespread format: WordPad and TextEdit produce it, many business programs use it when exporting letters or reports, and so do some note-taking apps. Turning it into a PDF stops each program from displaying it differently.

The conversion runs with LibreOffice Writer on our server, with no internet connection, and keeps everything RTF can store: fonts, bold and italics, colours, tables, embedded images, headers and footers. If the document uses heading styles, they become bookmarks for navigating the PDF.

You can pick PDF/A-2b, the format designed to preserve documents for years, or tagged PDF/UA for screen readers. If the RTF contains comments and you want them visible next to the text, turn on "Word: comments in margin" under more options. That is also where you set the quality and maximum resolution of images.

Use Pages to choose which parts of the result to keep, for example "1-4" or "even". Several RTF files can be converted at once; each gives its own PDF and, when there is more than one, a ZIP too. The maximum number of pages per document depends on your plan.

faq.q: Why does my RTF look different in another program?
faq.a: Every word processor interprets RTF in its own way, especially tables and margins. The PDF fixes the result so everyone sees the same thing.

faq.q: What happens to fonts that are not on the server?
faq.a: They are replaced with ones of equivalent metrics, so the text takes up the same space and the pagination does not shift.

faq.q: What if the file is plain text?
faq.a: For a TXT file use TXT to PDF, which detects the encoding and lets you choose the font and margins.
